source.title: Evaluating the wild Brauer group
source.venue: Inventiones mathematicae 234 (2023), no. 2, 819–891 (received 25 April 2022, accepted 11 July 2023, published online 8 August 2023)
readSections: The whole paper, §§1–11 and the references. Read 2026-09-22 from the arXiv v5 TeX source (e-print SHA-256 7e2175a306b5ceee089426154eb64f5175010fcd541a2ece8495c657e7cf59b1; PDF SHA-256 bc6926b9002f6d5a07a1c25647d3a60efaaf39f20553ecaf7f0c6a2a4d3f4fc1).

The published Inventiones PDF (73 pages, SHA-256 0e96ca755aa61e748bca722ea2c1107bed115575ff4fa8d6c751b721c33e79d2) was compared word by word with v5: statement numbering and text agree, and page locators below are the journal pages.

Checked in detail: Lemma 2.19's binomial estimates and Remark 2.20, the use of Lemma 2.16 in Corollary 9.8, Lemma 3.3, the residue computations of Lemmas 5.1 and 6.1, the first steps of the §8 blowup induction, all of §9 (Lemmas 9.1–9.5, Corollaries 9.4–9.8), the conductor computations of Lemmas 10.4–10.7 against Propositions 10.3, 10.8 and 10.9, Lemma 10.1 and Proposition 10.2, Lemmas 11.1–11.4, and the proofs of Theorems C and D. Kato's cited results ([K] Theorems 5.1, 7.1, 8.1, Propositions 6.1, 6.3, 7.3) and the Bloch–Kato inputs were used as quoted.

summary: Bright and Newton determine how precisely a p-adic point must be known to evaluate a Brauer class of p-power order on a variety X over a p-adic field k with smooth model 𝒳. The evaluation filtration Ev_n Br X (constancy on discs B(P, e(n+1)) over all finite extensions) equals a modification fil~_n of Kato's Swan conductor filtration: Ev_{−2} = ker ∂, Ev_{−1} = ∂^{−1}H¹(𝔽), Ev_0 = fil_0 and Ev_n = {A ∈ fil_{n+1} : rsw_{n+1}(A) ∈ [Ω², 0]} (Theorem A). The refined Swan conductor rsw_n(A) = [α, β] controls the variation on discs: inv A(Q) = inv A(P) + (1/p)Tr β_{P₀}(v_n(P, Q)) on B(P, n), and when β = 0 a bilinear formula in α_{P₀} governs the next discs (Theorems B and 8.1). The proof blows up 𝒳 at points of the special fibre repeatedly, following the Swan conductor along the exceptional divisors down to 0, where tame evaluation is read off the residue in H¹(Y, Q/Z). Applications: every good ordinary prime of a variety with H⁰(Ω²) ≠ 0 becomes involved in a Brauer–Manin obstruction to weak approximation after a finite extension (Theorem C, answering Swinnerton-Dyer's question negatively), and, when Pic V̄ is finitely generated and torsion-free, evaluation is constant outside an explicit finite set of places (Theorem D). §10 shows fil~ is not induced from H¹ and is neither of the Abbes–Saito filtrations. The atlas plans the local Brauer group and invariant (ClassFieldTheory Layer 5), the Brauer–Manin pairing (RP.2), de Rham–Witt complexes (CR.4) and the Cartier operator (DD.3). It has no Kato Swan conductor theory for imperfect residue fields, no Bloch–Kato p-adic vanishing cycles and no p-adic evaluation of Brauer classes. These are routed to two Part II candidates: the local theory (fil_n, λ_π, δ_r, rsw_n, Kato's geometric theorems, fil~_n and its comparison with Abbes–Saito) extends Local fields and ramification; the evaluation theory and its Brauer–Manin applications extend Heights, rational points and obstructions. General inputs go as sources to SF.2 (Gabber, proper base change, purity, Hochschild–Serre, Lemma 11.4), WC.5 (Lang–Weil) and RP.2. Seven source issues are recorded: five small misprints and slips in §§6, 9, 10, an over-broad hypothesis in the proof of Proposition 10.9, and the introduction's claim that Theorem C answers Wittenberg's Question 1.4, which needs a prime of good ordinary reduction. Independent review REV-PAPER-BRIGHT-NEWTON-23 requires revision: corrected coefficient twists, scopes and source defects; atomic dependency closure and routes 2, 4 and 5 remain incomplete. Four pinned-library prerequisites are now inventoried explicitly. The 2025 Ambrosi–Newton–Pagano sequel resolves the general weak-approximation question by a different argument.

items.name: p-adic discs B(P, r) and the evaluation filtration Ev_n Br X
items.statement: Setting of §§1, 3, 7–9: k is a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers O_k, uniformiser π, residue field 𝔽 and absolute ramification index e, and e′ = ep/(p−1). X/k is smooth and geometrically irreducible, 𝒳 → Spec O_k is a smooth model of X (not assumed proper) whose special fibre Y is geometrically irreducible, F is the function field of Y and K^h is the fraction field of a Henselisation of O_{𝒳,Y}. For a finite extension k′/k with ramification index e(k′/k), uniformiser π′, r ≥ 1 and P ∈ 𝒳(O_{k′}), B(P, r) is the set of Q ∈ 𝒳(O_{k′}) with the same image as P in 𝒳(O_{k′}/(π′)^r). For A ∈ Br X let |A| : 𝒳(O_{k′}) → Br k′ be evaluation. Then Ev_n Br X = {A : for all finite k′/k and all P ∈ 𝒳(O_{k′}), |A| is constant on B(P, e(k′/k)(n+1))} for n ≥ 0; Ev_{−1} Br X = {A : |A| is constant on 𝒳(O_{k′}) for all finite k′/k}; Ev_{−2} Br X = {A : |A| is zero on 𝒳(O_{k′}) for all finite k′/k}.
items.locator: Theorem A, p. 820, definitions before Theorem A, pp. 819–820
items.note: The object the paper classifies. Kato's filtration fil_n Br X and rsw_n are pulled back from Br K^h.

items.name: Theorem A(1): Ev_{−2} Br X = ker ∂
items.statement: Setting of §§1, 3, 7–9: k is a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers O_k, uniformiser π, residue field 𝔽 and absolute ramification index e, and e′ = ep/(p−1). X/k is smooth and geometrically irreducible, 𝒳 → Spec O_k is a smooth model of X (not assumed proper) whose special fibre Y is geometrically irreducible, F is the function field of Y and K^h is the fraction field of a Henselisation of O_{𝒳,Y}. Then Ev_{−2} Br X = {A ∈ fil_0 Br X : ∂A = 0}, where ∂ : fil_0 Br X → H¹(Y, Q/Z) is the residue map of Proposition 3.1.
items.note: Proved in §9 (Corollary 9.7). By Corollary 3.7 the right side is the image of Br 𝒳.

items.name: Theorem A(2): Ev_{−1} Br X = ∂^{−1}(H¹(𝔽, Q/Z))
items.statement: Setting of §§1, 3, 7–9: k is a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers O_k, uniformiser π, residue field 𝔽 and absolute ramification index e, and e′ = ep/(p−1). X/k is smooth and geometrically irreducible, 𝒳 → Spec O_k is a smooth model of X (not assumed proper) whose special fibre Y is geometrically irreducible, F is the function field of Y and K^h is the fraction field of a Henselisation of O_{𝒳,Y}. Then Ev_{−1} Br X = {A ∈ fil_0 Br X : ∂A ∈ H¹(𝔽, Q/Z)}.
items.note: Proved in §9 (Corollary 9.7), via Proposition 3.1 and Lemma 9.5.

items.name: Theorem A(3): Ev_0 Br X = fil_0 Br X
items.statement: Setting of §§1, 3, 7–9: k is a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers O_k, uniformiser π, residue field 𝔽 and absolute ramification index e, and e′ = ep/(p−1). X/k is smooth and geometrically irreducible, 𝒳 → Spec O_k is a smooth model of X (not assumed proper) whose special fibre Y is geometrically irreducible, F is the function field of Y and K^h is the fraction field of a Henselisation of O_{𝒳,Y}. Then Ev_0 Br X = fil_0 Br X.
items.note: Corollary 9.4 with n = 0.

items.name: Theorem A(4): Ev_n Br X for n ≥ 1 via the refined Swan conductor
items.statement: Setting of §§1, 3, 7–9: k is a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers O_k, uniformiser π, residue field 𝔽 and absolute ramification index e, and e′ = ep/(p−1). X/k is smooth and geometrically irreducible, 𝒳 → Spec O_k is a smooth model of X (not assumed proper) whose special fibre Y is geometrically irreducible, F is the function field of Y and K^h is the fraction field of a Henselisation of O_{𝒳,Y}. For n ≥ 1, Ev_n Br X = {A ∈ fil_{n+1} Br X : rsw_{n+1}(A) ∈ [Ω²_F, 0]_{π,n+1}}, i.e. A has Swan conductor at most n+1 and, if it is n+1, its refined Swan conductor has β-component 0. The same equalities hold if only unramified k′/k are allowed in the definition of Ev_n (Corollaries 9.4 and 9.7).
items.note: Corollary 9.4. The right side is fil~_n Br X, the modified filtration of item PAPER-BRIGHT-NEWTON-23/82.

items.name: Question 1.3 (Swinnerton-Dyer): the Brauer–Manin set involves only bad places
items.statement: Define the following proposition/problem (not an asserted theorem): Let L be a number field, S a finite set of places containing the archimedean ones, 𝒱 a smooth projective O_S-scheme with geometrically integral fibres and generic fibre V, and assume Pic V̄ is finitely generated and torsion-free. Is there an open and closed Z ⊂ ∏_{v∈S} V(L_v) with V(A_L)^{Br} = Z × ∏_{v∉S} V(L_v)?
items.note: Question 1.3 is answered negatively in general by Theorem C (for example K3 surfaces). This item defines the question, not a goal to prove its false universal assertion.

items.name: Question 1.4 (Wittenberg): Hasse principle and weak approximation over all finite extensions force H²(V, O_V) = 0?
items.statement: Define the following proposition/problem (not an asserted theorem): If a smooth projective variety V over a number field L satisfies the Hasse principle and weak approximation over all finite extensions of L, does it follow that H²(V, O_V) = 0?
items.note: The 2023 argument answers this under existence of a good ordinary prime; see E7. Ambrosi–Newton–Pagano, arXiv:2509.22025, Corollary 1.1.2, proves the stronger weak-approximation-only conclusion H⁰(Ω²)=0; for smooth projective characteristic-zero varieties Hodge symmetry gives H²(O)=0. This later result is not attributed to Bright–Newton or assumed proved here.

items.name: Theorem C: potential failure of weak approximation at good ordinary primes
items.statement: Let V be a smooth proper variety over a number field L with H⁰(V, Ω²_V) ≠ 0. Let 𝔭 be a prime of L at which V has good ordinary reduction, with residue characteristic p. Then there exist a finite extension L′/L, a prime 𝔭′ of L′ above 𝔭 and A ∈ Br V_{L′}{p} such that |A| : V(L′_{𝔭′}) → Br L′_{𝔭′} is non-constant. In particular, if V(A_{L′}) ≠ ∅ then A obstructs weak approximation on V_{L′}.
items.locator: Theorem C, p. 823, proof in §11, pp. 887–888
items.note: Proof: Bloch–Kato's ordinary theorem gives α ∈ H²(V̄, Z/p^r) with non-zero image in gr⁰ of the vanishing-cycle filtration; Lemma 3.4 shows its image in Br K^h is not in fil_0; Theorem A(3) then gives non-constancy over a finite extension.

items.name: Question 1.5: a finite set of places controlling the Brauer–Manin set
items.statement: Define the following proposition/problem (not an asserted theorem): Let V be a smooth, proper, geometrically irreducible variety over a number field L with Pic V̄ finitely generated and torsion-free. Is there a finite set S of places of L and a closed Z ⊂ ∏_{v∈S} V(L_v) with V(A_L)^{Br} = Z × ∏_{v∉S} V(L_v)? If so, can S be described explicitly?
items.note: Answered positively by Theorem D. The torsion-freeness hypothesis is necessary (elliptic curves with finite Sha and trivial Mordell–Weil group; Harari's descent obstruction when π₁^ét(V̄) ≠ 0). This is a problem definition; Theorem D, item 10, supplies the positive answer.

items.name: Theorem D: evaluation is constant outside an explicit finite set of places
items.statement: Let L be a number field and V a smooth, proper, geometrically irreducible variety over L with Pic V̄ finitely generated and torsion-free. Then there is a finite set S of places of L such that for all A ∈ Br V and all 𝔭 ∉ S, |A| : V(L_𝔭) → Br L_𝔭 is constant. S can be taken to be: (1) the archimedean places; (2) the places of bad reduction; (3) the places 𝔭 with e_𝔭 ≥ p − 1, where e_𝔭 is the absolute ramification index and p the residue characteristic; (4) the places 𝔭 such that, for any smooth proper model 𝒱 → Spec O_𝔭, H⁰(𝒱(𝔭), Ω¹_{𝒱(𝔭)}) ≠ 0.
items.locator: Theorem D, p. 824, proof in §11, pp. 888–889
items.note: Proof: Lemmas 11.2–11.4 for the p-part and [CTSk, Proposition 2.4] for the prime-to-p part.

items.name: Remark 1.6(1) (J. Newton): the places in Theorem D(4) are ramified or lie above 2
items.statement: In Theorem D, if 𝔭 has e_{𝔭/p} = 1 and residue characteristic p > 2, then H⁰(𝒱(𝔭), Ω¹) = 0: H¹_ét(V̄, Z/p) = 0 because Pic V̄ is torsion-free, so H¹_dR(𝒱(𝔭)/𝔽_𝔭) = 0 by the integral comparison theorem of Fontaine–Messing (see Breuil–Messing, Theorems 3.1.3.1 and 3.2.3), and the Hodge–de Rham spectral sequence of 𝒱(𝔭) degenerates (Deligne–Illusie, Corollary 2.5).
items.note: Retain this remark as a required target, with Fontaine–Messing integral comparison (Breuil–Messing Theorems 3.1.3.1 and 3.2.3) and Deligne–Illusie Corollary 2.5 as explicit source-acquisition and owner-audit gaps. DD.3's warning about hypotheses is not a proof that the atlas lacks an owner. Route 5 is rejected until those inputs are assigned.

items.name: The local Brauer group of k: inv and the residue isomorphism
items.statement: For k finite over Q_p: inv : Br k → Q/Z is an isomorphism, Br k[p^t] ≅ p^{−t}Z/Z, the residue ∂ : Br k → H¹(𝔽, Q/Z) is an isomorphism (Br k = Br(k^{nr}/k)), and res_{k′/k} multiplies inv by [k′ : k].
items.note: ClassFieldTheory Layer 5 constructs Br F = H²(G_F, (F^s)^×) with the invariant map normalised on unramified layers, and the degree-multiplying restriction square.

items.name: The Brauer–Manin pairing and the sets V(A_L)^B ⊇ V(A_L)^{Br}
items.statement: For V smooth, proper, geometrically irreducible over a number field L, the local evaluation maps give a pairing Br V × V(A_L) → Q/Z whose right kernel V(A_L)^{Br} contains V(L); V(A_L)^B is the set of adelic points orthogonal to a given B ∈ Br V.
items.note: RP.2 plans restricted adelic points, local invariants and the Brauer–Manin pairing.

items.name: Non-constant local evaluation obstructs weak approximation
items.statement: Let V be smooth, proper and geometrically irreducible over a number field L, with V(A_L) nonempty, and B ∈ Br V of order n. If a finite place 𝔭 has surjective evaluation V(L_𝔭) → Br L_𝔭[n], then V(A_L)^B is nonempty; if also n > 1, it is a proper subset of V(A_L). Thus B alone does not obstruct the Hasse principle, and for n > 1 obstructs weak approximation. More generally nonconstant local evaluation at one place gives a proper Brauer–Manin subset and obstructs weak approximation, still assuming V(A_L) nonempty.
items.note: A general Brauer–Manin test at one place, used for Theorem C. The n>1 condition repairs the trivial-class edge case E14.

items.name: Logarithmic de Rham–Witt sheaves and Illusie's F − 1 sequence
items.statement: For a scheme S smooth over a field of characteristic p (and for fields such as F and F(T)): the de Rham–Witt complex W_rΩ^•_S with Frobenius F, Verschiebung V and dlog; the logarithmic subsheaf W_rΩ^q_{S,log} ⊂ W_rΩ^q_S generated étale locally by dlog[a₁] ∧ … ∧ dlog[a_q]; and the exact sequence 0 → W_rΩ^{q−1}_log → W_rΩ^{q−1} →(C^{−1} − 1)→ W_rΩ^{q−1}/dV^{r−1}Ω^{q−2} → 0 on R_ét (Illusie I.3.3, I.3.23; Kato §1.3), where C^{−1} is Illusie's F, equal to the inverse Cartier operator for r = 1.
items.note: CR.4 constructs W_nΩ with F, V, restriction, Teichmüller lifts and dlog, localisation and étale descent; HL.2 introduces logarithmic de Rham–Witt coefficients. The paper needs them over function fields over finite fields and their Henselisations, i.e. localisations of smooth algebras over perfect fields.

items.name: The Cartier operator C on closed forms
items.statement: For a field ℓ of characteristic p, C : Z Ω^q_ℓ → Ω^q_ℓ on closed forms, inverse to C^{−1}(a dlog b₁ ∧ …) = a^p dlog b₁ ∧ …, with C(dΩ^{q−1}) = 0.
items.note: DD.3 compares the derived Cartier theory with classical Cartier on smooth algebras; CR.4 supplies it through de Rham–Witt. Fields finitely generated over a perfect field are colimits of smooth algebras.

items.name: Kato's coefficients (Z/n)(r) and the groups H^q_n(R), H^q(R)
items.statement: Write n = p^s m with p ∤ m. For S smooth over a field of characteristic p, (Z/n)(r) = μ_m^{⊗r} ⊕ W_sΩ^r_{S,log}[−r] in D^b(S_ét); in other cases (n invertible) it is the usual twist. H^q_n(R) = H^q(R_ét, (Z/n)(q−1)) and H^q(R) = colim_n H^q_n(R). There is an exact triangle (Z/n)(1) → G_m →(n) G_m → (Z/n)(1)[1] (Kummer, and Illusie I.3.23.2 in characteristic p), so H²(K) = Br K for every field K.
items.note: Kato's notation [K, §1]. Needed in equal characteristic (Henselised function fields of varieties in characteristic p) and in mixed characteristic.

items.name: The groups V^q_n(A), their functoriality and products
items.statement: If char K > 0, additionally suppose A⊗_{O_K}K is smooth over a field, as in §2.1. For a ring A over O_K (K a Henselian discrete valuation field with residue field F of characteristic p), with i, j the inclusions of the special and generic fibres and R = A/m_K A: V^q_n(A) = H^q(R_ét, i*Rj_*(Z/n)(q−1)) and V^q(A) = colim_n V^q_n(A). They are functorial for maps (O_K → A) → (O_{K′} → A′); V^q_n(O_K) = H^q_n(K) when char K = 0; V^q_n(A) ≅ V^q_n(A^{(h)}) ≅ H^q_n(A^{(h)} ⊗ K) for the Henselisation along m_K A; and there are products V^q(A) × ((A ⊗ K)^×)^r → V^{q+r}(A), {χ, a₁, …, a_r}.
items.note: Uses Gabber's affine proper base change (routed to SF.2). i*Rj_* is the non-geometric nearby-cycle complex; LPV.0's RΨ is its strict-Henselian version. This is a bundle requiring separation into carrier, functoriality, comparison and products; geometric/non-geometric descent is a bridge to be built, not an identification by terminology.

items.name: Gabber's affine analogue of proper base change
items.statement: If (A, I) is a Henselian pair and 𝓕 is a torsion étale sheaf on Spec A, then H^q(Spec A, 𝓕) → H^q(Spec A/I, 𝓕|) is an isomorphism; in particular H^q_n(A ⊗_{O_K} K) → V^q_n(A) is an isomorphism when (A, m_K A) is Henselian.
items.note: A general theorem of étale cohomology of schemes.

items.name: Definition 2.1 (Kato): the Swan conductor filtration fil_n H^q(K)
items.statement: For a Henselian discrete valuation field K with residue field of characteristic p > 0 and uniformiser π: χ ∈ fil_n H^q(K) ⟺ {χ, 1 + π^{n+1}T} = 0 in V^{q+1}(O_K[T]). sw(χ) is the least n ≥ 0 with χ ∈ fil_n H^q(K). By [K, Proposition 1.8] V^{q+1}_{p^r}(O_K[T]) → V^{q+1}(O_K[T]) is injective, so the same test can be made at level p^r (Remark 2.2).

items.name: Kato's Galois-cohomological characterisation of fil_n (Remark 2.3)
items.statement: χ ∈ H^q(K) lies in fil_n H^q(K) iff for every Henselian discrete valuation field L ⊇ K with O_K ⊂ O_L and m_L = O_L m_K, {χ_L, 1 + π^{n+1}O_L} = 0 in H^{q+1}(L).
items.note: Used for base change (Lemma 2.16).

items.name: Remark 2.4: for q = 1 and K/Q_p finite, fil_n is the upper-numbering filtration
items.statement: If K is a finite extension of Q_p, the filtration fil_n on H¹(K) = Hom(Gal(K̄/K), Q/Z) coincides with the one induced by the upper ramification filtration (via local reciprocity, which matches upper ramification groups with unit groups).
items.note: The compatibility with the classical perfect-residue-field theory.

items.name: Kato's canonical lifting ι^q_n and λ_π
items.statement: For a Henselian local ring A with fraction field L and residue field ℓ of characteristic p: ι^q_n : H^q_n(ℓ) → H^q_n(L), defined via H^q(A_ét) for p ∤ n and, for n = p^s, by ι^q_n({χ, ā₁, …, ā_{q−1}}) = {ι¹_n(χ), a₁, …, a_{q−1}} (Kato proves this is well defined). For a Henselian DVF K with uniformiser π, λ_π : H^q_n(F) ⊕ H^{q−1}_n(F) → H^q_n(K), λ_π(χ, χ′) = ι^q_n(χ) + {ι^{q−1}_n(χ′), π}, is injective.

items.name: Proposition 2.6 (Kato, Proposition 6.1): fil_0 and the image of λ_π
items.statement: Let p = char F > 0. (1) fil_0 H^q(K) is the image of λ_π, and fil_0 H^q(K) = H^q(K)(non-p) ⊕ ker(H^q(K){p} → H^q(K_nr){p}). (2) H^q(K) = fil_0 H^q(K) if [F : F^p] = p^c < ∞ and q > c + 1.
items.note: With Grothendieck's Brauer III, Corollaire 1.3, fil_0 Br X is the set of classes split by an unramified extension of K^h (§3).

items.name: Bloch–Kato: the filtration U^m on p-adic vanishing cycles and its graded pieces
items.statement: For A smooth over O_K with char K = 0 and R = A/m_K A, the sheaves M^q_r = i*R^q j_*(Z/p^r)(q) carry Bloch–Kato's decreasing filtration U^m, with gr⁰ M^q_r ≅ W_rΩ^q_{R,log} ⊕ W_rΩ^{q−1}_{R,log} ([BK, Theorem 1.4], [K, §1]). R has p-cohomological dimension ≤ 1 (SGA 4 X.5.1), so the spectral sequence for V^q_{p^r}(A) gives 0 → H¹(R_ét, M^{q−1}_r) → V^q_{p^r}(A) → H⁰(R_ét, i*R^q j_*((Z/p^r)(q−1))) → 0.
items.note: The local structure theorem of p-adic vanishing cycles, the input of λ_π for smooth A (Lemma 2.7) and of Lemma 3.4. The last term has twist q−1, unlike the separately defined M^q_r with twist q. The extraction, not equation (2.4) of the source, had this error.

items.name: Lemma 2.7: H¹ of M^{q−1}_r sees only gr⁰
items.statement: Let A be smooth over O_K, char K=0, R=A/m_KA, and r≥1. Suppose q ≥ 2. The natural map H¹(R_ét, M^{q−1}_r) → H¹(R_ét, gr⁰M^{q−1}_r) ≅ H¹(R_ét, W_rΩ^{q−1}_{R,log} ⊕ W_rΩ^{q−2}_{R,log}) is an isomorphism.

items.name: Definition 2.8: λ_π and ι^q_{p^r} for A smooth over O_K
items.statement: Suppose char K = 0 and q ≥ 2. λ_π : H^q_{p^r}(R) ⊕ H^{q−1}_{p^r}(R) → V^q_{p^r}(A) is (−1)^{q−1} times the inverse of the isomorphism of Lemma 2.7 followed by H¹(R_ét, M^{q−1}_r) → V^q_{p^r}(A); ι^q_{p^r} : H^q_{p^r}(R) → V^q_{p^r}(A) is its first component. Here A is smooth over O_K and R=A/m_KA. For A=O_K, Remark 2.9 describes the Hochschild–Serre edge map H¹(F,H^{q−1}(K_nr,(Z/p^r)(q−1))) → H^q(K,(Z/p^r)(q−1)); it is not the usual inflation H^q(F,−) → H^q(K,−).

items.name: Definition 2.10: δ_r : W_rΩ^{q−1}_R → H^q_{p^r}(R)
items.statement: δ_r : W_rΩ^{q−1}_R/dV^{r−1}Ω^{q−2}_R → H^q_{p^r}(R) = H¹(R_ét, W_rΩ^{q−1}_log) is the boundary map of the sequence 0 → W_rΩ^{q−1}_log → W_rΩ^{q−1} → W_rΩ^{q−1}/dV^{r−1}Ω^{q−2} → 0; also δ_r denotes its composite with the quotient map from W_rΩ^{q−1}_R. For q = 1, r = 1 it is the Artin–Schreier map F → H¹(F, Z/p).
items.note: Kato writes λ_π for λ_π ∘ δ_r ((2.5)).

items.name: Lemma 2.11: δ_r(w ∧ dlog a) = δ_r(w) ∪ {a}
items.statement: Let w ∈ W_rΩ^{q−1}_R and a ∈ R^×, and let f_a : H^q_{p^r}(R) → H^{q+1}_{p^r}(R) be induced by x ↦ x ∧ dlog(a) on W_rΩ_log. Then δ_r(w ∧ dlog(a)) = f_a(δ_r(w)) = δ_r(w) ∪ {a}.

items.name: Lemma 2.12: the two definitions of λ_π agree
items.statement: When char K = 0, A = O_K and q ≥ 2, the map λ_π of Definition 2.8 agrees with λ_π(χ, χ′) = ι^q(χ) + {ι^{q−1}(χ′), π} of §2.2.2.
items.note: Uses [K3, §1.2, Lemma 2(2)] (Kato's local class field theory II) and [BK, after Corollary 1.4.1].

items.name: Lemma 2.13: base change of λ_π
items.statement: Assume char K=0. Let (O_K → A) → (O_{K′} → A′) be a map as in §2.1 with A, A′ smooth, e the ramification index of K′/K and ā ∈ F′ the reduction of φ(π)(π′)^{−e}. For q ≥ 2 and r ≥ 1, φ_* ∘ λ_π ∘ δ_r = λ_{π′} ∘ δ_r ∘ ((α, β) ↦ (φ̄_*α + φ̄_*β ∧ dlog ā, e φ̄_*β)) on W_rΩ^{q−1}_R ⊕ W_rΩ^{q−2}_R, and likewise with (α, β) ↦ (φ̄_*α + {φ̄_*β, ā}, e φ̄_*β) on H^q_{p^r}(R) ⊕ H^{q−1}_{p^r}(R).

items.name: Kato, Theorem 5.1: existence and uniqueness of (α, β)
items.statement: If χ ∈ fil_n H^q(K) with n ≥ 1, there is a unique (α, β) ∈ Ω^q_F ⊕ Ω^{q−1}_F with {χ, 1 + π^n T} = λ_π(Tα, Tβ) in V^{q+1}(O_K[T]) (λ_π meaning λ_π ∘ δ₁ for O_K[T]); χ ∈ fil_{n−1} iff (α, β) = 0.

items.name: Definition 2.14: the refined Swan conductor rsw_n
items.statement: Let ω¹_F be the module of absolute log differentials of the standard log point on F induced by O_K, with formal dlog π. Put ω^q_F=∧^q_F ω¹_F, with 0 → Ω^q_F → ω^q_F →(res) Ω^{q−1}_F → 0 split by η ↦ η ∧ dlog π. For χ ∈ fil_n H^q(K), n ≥ 1, rsw_n(χ) = π^{−n}(α + β ∧ dlog π) ∈ m_K^{−n} ⊗_{O_K} ω^q_F with (α, β) as in Kato's Theorem 5.1, written [α, β]_{π,n}. It is an injection fil_n/fil_{n−1} → m_K^{−n} ⊗ ω^q_F, and the pair (α, β) depends on π (Remark 2.15).
items.note: Use the standard-log-point construction (Borger §4.5), not the erroneous fractional-differential carrier on p.837; see E9. For a chosen π the degree-one presentation over O_K is (Ω¹_{O_K} ⊕ O_K·ℓ)/(dπ−πℓ); reduction gives Ω¹_F ⊕ F·ℓ. Ordinary Kähler differentials are a pinned-library input, item 114. The log enhancement, residue sequence and exterior differential still need explicit suppliers.

items.name: Lemma 2.16: base change of fil_n and rsw_n
items.statement: Suppose char K = 0. Let K′/K be a finite extension of Henselian DVFs with ramification index e, π′ a uniformiser of K′ and ā ∈ F′ the reduction of π(π′)^{−e}. If χ ∈ fil_n H^q(K) then res(χ) ∈ fil_{en} H^q(K′), and for n ≥ 1, if rsw_n(χ) = [α, β]_{π,n} then rsw_{en}(res χ) = [ā^{−n}(α + β ∧ dlog ā), ā^{−n} e β]_{π′,en}.

items.name: Lemma 2.17: dα = 0 and dβ = (−1)^q nα
items.statement: If χ ∈ fil_n H^q(K) and rsw_n(χ) = [α, β]_{π,n}, then dα = 0 and dβ = (−1)^q nα. In particular if p ∤ n and β = 0 then α = 0.
items.note: Implicit in [K, Proposition 5.4], which is stated without proof; the paper supplies one.

items.name: Lemma 2.18: two identities for δ₁ over F(T)
items.statement: Let R = F(T) and α ∈ Ω^{q−1}_F with q ≥ 2. (1) δ₁(T dα) = (−1)^q {δ₁(Tα), T} in H^{q+1}_p(R). (2) If dα = 0 then δ₁(T C(α)) = δ₁(T^p α).

items.name: Lemma 2.19: Swan conductor of pχ
items.statement: Suppose char K = 0, e = v_K(p), e′ = ep/(p−1), u = p/π^e with reduction ū ∈ F^×. Let sw(χ) = n > 0 and rsw_n(χ) = [α, β]_{π,n}. (1) If n ≥ e′ − 1 then pχ ∈ fil_{n−e} H^q(K). (2) If n > e′ then rsw_{n−e}(pχ) = [ūα, ūβ]_{π,n−e}, so sw(pχ) = n − e. (3) If n = e′ then dα = dβ = 0 and rsw_{e′−e}(pχ) = [ūα + C(α), ūβ + C(β)]_{π,e′−e}. Consequently (Remark 2.20), if β ∧ dū = 0 and sw(χ) > e′ then eα = 0.

items.name: Definition 2.21: the residue map ∂ on fil_0
items.statement: ∂ : fil_0 H^q_n(K) → H^{q−1}_n(F) is λ_π^{−1} followed by projection to the second factor; its colimit is ∂ : fil_0 H^q(K) → H^{q−1}(F).

items.name: Proposition 2.22: ∂ agrees with the classical Brauer residue
items.statement: Assume char K=0 as in §2.5. For every n ≥ 1 the diagram H²_n(F) →(ι²_n) fil_0 H²_n(K) →(∂) H¹_n(F) maps, via the Kummer triangle and Z/n ⊂ Q/Z, to Br F →(ι′) Br(K_nr/K) →(∂′) H¹(F, Q/Z), and commutes; here 0 → Br F → Br(K_nr/K) → H¹(F, Q/Z) → 0 is the classical residue sequence.

items.name: Lemma 2.23: δχ ∪ a = t(χ ∪ u(a))
items.statement: Let L be a field and n ≥ 1, u : L^× → H¹(L, (Z/n)(1)) and t : H²(L, (Z/n)(1)) → Br L from the triangle (1.3), and δ : H¹(L, Z/n) → H²(L, Z) the connecting map of 0 → Z → Z → Z/n → 0. For χ ∈ H¹(L, Z/n) and a ∈ L^×, δχ ∪ a = t(χ ∪ u(a)).
items.note: Including the p-part in characteristic p ([GS, Proposition 3.4.8]).

items.name: Proposition 3.1(1): residues of tame classes are unramified on Y
items.statement: Setting of §§1, 3, 7–9: k is a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers O_k, uniformiser π, residue field 𝔽 and absolute ramification index e, and e′ = ep/(p−1). X/k is smooth and geometrically irreducible, 𝒳 → Spec O_k is a smooth model of X (not assumed proper) whose special fibre Y is geometrically irreducible, F is the function field of Y and K^h is the fraction field of a Henselisation of O_{𝒳,Y}. ∂ also denotes fil_0 Br X → fil_0 H²(K^h) →(∂) H¹(F). If A ∈ fil_0 Br X then ∂(A) ∈ H¹(Y, Q/Z) ⊂ H¹(F, Q/Z).

items.name: Proposition 3.1(2): tame evaluation through the residue
items.statement: Setting of §§1, 3, 7–9: k is a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers O_k, uniformiser π, residue field 𝔽 and absolute ramification index e, and e′ = ep/(p−1). X/k is smooth and geometrically irreducible, 𝒳 → Spec O_k is a smooth model of X (not assumed proper) whose special fibre Y is geometrically irreducible, F is the function field of Y and K^h is the fraction field of a Henselisation of O_{𝒳,Y}. Let P ∈ 𝒳(O_k) reduce to P₀ ∈ Y(𝔽). Then ∂(P*A) = P₀*(∂A) for A ∈ fil_0 Br X, where ∂ : Br k → H¹(𝔽, Q/Z) is the residue isomorphism.

items.name: Corollary 3.2: tame classes evaluate through the special fibre
items.statement: Setting of §§1, 3, 7–9: k is a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers O_k, uniformiser π, residue field 𝔽 and absolute ramification index e, and e′ = ep/(p−1). X/k is smooth and geometrically irreducible, 𝒳 → Spec O_k is a smooth model of X (not assumed proper) whose special fibre Y is geometrically irreducible, F is the function field of Y and K^h is the fraction field of a Henselisation of O_{𝒳,Y}. (i) For A ∈ fil_0 Br X, |A| : 𝒳(O_k) → Br k depends only on ∂(A). (ii) For A ∈ fil_0 Br X and P ∈ X(k) reducing to a smooth point P₀ ∈ Y(𝔽), A(P) depends only on P₀.

items.name: Lemma 3.3: inv via Artin–Schreier and trace
items.statement: Let δ₁ : 𝔽 → H¹(𝔽, Z/p) be the Artin–Schreier map. If A ∈ Br k[p] has ∂(A) = (1/p)δ₁(x) with x ∈ 𝔽, then inv(A) = (1/p)Tr_{𝔽/𝔽_p}(x).
items.note: The source of the trace in Theorem 8.1(2).

items.name: Lemma 3.4: vanishing-cycle sheaves inject into their generic stalks
items.statement: Setting of §§1, 3, 7–9: k is a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers O_k, uniformiser π, residue field 𝔽 and absolute ramification index e, and e′ = ep/(p−1). X/k is smooth and geometrically irreducible, 𝒳 → Spec O_k is a smooth model of X (not assumed proper) whose special fibre Y is geometrically irreducible, F is the function field of Y and K^h is the fraction field of a Henselisation of O_{𝒳,Y}. Let i : Y → 𝒳, j : X → 𝒳 and τ : Spec F → Y be the inclusions, q, r ≥ 1. Then i*R^q j_*(Z/p^r)(q−1) → τ_*τ* i*R^q j_*(Z/p^r)(q−1) is injective.
items.note: Proof uses Bloch–Kato Proposition 6.1(i), surjectivity of Galois symbols from their §5, and induction on r. The original extraction's attribution to Gabber 1993 was incorrect. Used in Lemma 3.5 and Theorem C.

items.name: Lemma 3.5: integrality of tame classes
items.statement: Setting of §§1, 3, 7–9: k is a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers O_k, uniformiser π, residue field 𝔽 and absolute ramification index e, and e′ = ep/(p−1). X/k is smooth and geometrically irreducible, 𝒳 → Spec O_k is a smooth model of X (not assumed proper) whose special fibre Y is geometrically irreducible, F is the function field of Y and K^h is the fraction field of a Henselisation of O_{𝒳,Y}. Suppose 𝒳 = Spec A is affine and R = A/m_k A. Let r ≥ 1, q ≥ 2 and χ ∈ fil_0 H^q_{p^r}(K^h), so χ = λ_π(α, β) for unique (α, β) ∈ H^q_{p^r}(F) ⊕ H^{q−1}_{p^r}(F). If χ lies in the image of V^q_{p^r}(A), then (α, β) lies in the image of H^q_{p^r}(R) ⊕ H^{q−1}_{p^r}(R).

items.name: Lemma 3.6: unramified Brauer classes along Y
items.statement: Setting of §§1, 3, 7–9: k is a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers O_k, uniformiser π, residue field 𝔽 and absolute ramification index e, and e′ = ep/(p−1). X/k is smooth and geometrically irreducible, 𝒳 → Spec O_k is a smooth model of X (not assumed proper) whose special fibre Y is geometrically irreducible, F is the function field of Y and K^h is the fraction field of a Henselisation of O_{𝒳,Y}. K is the function field of X. The kernel of the classical residue ∂′ : fil_0 Br K → H¹(F, Q/Z) (fil_0 Br K = Br(K^h_nr/K)) is the image of Br O_{𝒳,Y} → Br K.
items.note: Generalises [CTSD, §1.1] to imperfect residue fields.

items.name: Purity for the Brauer group (Česnavičius; Gabber in this case)
items.statement: In the §3 setup, k/Q_p is finite and 𝒳/O_k is a smooth model of a smooth geometrically irreducible X/k with geometrically irreducible special fibre Y and common function field K. Then Br 𝒳 = Br X ∩ Br O_{𝒳,Y} inside Br K.
items.locator: Proof of Corollary 3.7, p. 848 ([Česnavičius 2019, Theorem 1.2]; [Gabber 1993, Theorem 2.2])
items.note: PAPER-CESNAVICIUS-19 routes Brauer purity to SF.2.

items.name: Corollary 3.7: ker ∂ = image of Br 𝒳
items.statement: Setting of §§1, 3, 7–9: k is a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers O_k, uniformiser π, residue field 𝔽 and absolute ramification index e, and e′ = ep/(p−1). X/k is smooth and geometrically irreducible, 𝒳 → Spec O_k is a smooth model of X (not assumed proper) whose special fibre Y is geometrically irreducible, F is the function field of Y and K^h is the fraction field of a Henselisation of O_{𝒳,Y}. The kernel of ∂ : fil_0 Br X → H¹(Y, Q/Z) is the image of Br 𝒳 → Br X. With Theorem A(1), Ev_{−2} Br X is the image of Br 𝒳 (a new proof, for smooth 𝒳, of a result of Saito–Sato).

items.name: Swan conductors along divisors of a normal scheme
items.statement: For a normal irreducible scheme X with function field K, χ ∈ H^q(K) and 𝔭 ∈ X¹, K_𝔭 = Frac(O^h_{X,𝔭}); sw_𝔭(χ) = sw(χ_𝔭) and, if sw_𝔭(χ) ≤ n with n ≥ 1, rsw_{𝔭,n}(χ) = rsw_n(χ_𝔭). For a prime divisor Z with generic point z, sw_Z = sw_z and rsw_{Z,n} = rsw_{z,n}. Separately, for a normal irreducible X, χ is unramified on X if for EVERY point x∈X its image in H^q(Frac O^h_{X,x}) lies in the image of the canonical ι^q:H^q(κ(x))→H^q(Frac O^h_{X,x}), as in §4.1. Do not replace this all-point condition by a codimension-one condition without a purity theorem.
items.note: Kato 1989, Part II.

items.name: Theorem 4.1 (Kato, Theorem 7.1): integrality of the refined Swan conductor
items.statement: Setting of §4.3: A is an excellent regular local ring with fraction field K and residue field ℓ of characteristic p with [ℓ : ℓ^p] = p^c; π₁, …, π_r is part of a regular system of parameters, 𝔭_i = π_iA, R_i = A/𝔭_i, D_j = Σ_{i≠j} V(𝔭_i) ∩ V(𝔭_j) on Spec R_j; χ ∈ H^q(K) is unramified outside ∪ V(𝔭_i) and n_i = sw_{𝔭_i}(χ). If n_j ≥ 1 and rsw_{𝔭_j}(χ) = (∏_i π_i^{−n_i})(α + β ∧ dlog π_j) with α ∈ Ω^q_{κ(𝔭_j)}, β ∈ Ω^{q−1}_{κ(𝔭_j)}, then α ∈ Ω^q_{R_j}(log D_j) and β ∈ Ω^{q−1}_{R_j}(log D_j).
items.note: Gives Theorem 8.1(1) (regularity of α, β at P₀).

items.name: Proposition 4.2 (Kato, Proposition 7.3): compatibility of the forms ω_s(j)
items.statement: Setting of §4.3: A is an excellent regular local ring with fraction field K and residue field ℓ of characteristic p with [ℓ : ℓ^p] = p^c; π₁, …, π_r is part of a regular system of parameters, 𝔭_i = π_iA, R_i = A/𝔭_i, D_j = Σ_{i≠j} V(𝔭_i) ∩ V(𝔭_j) on Spec R_j; χ ∈ H^q(K) is unramified outside ∪ V(𝔭_i) and n_i = sw_{𝔭_i}(χ). Let R = A/(𝔭₁ + ⋯ + 𝔭_r) and j₁, j₂ with n_{j₁}, n_{j₂} ≥ 1. For each s ⊂ {1, …, r}, the images of ω_s(j₁) and ω_s(j₂) in Ω^{q−|s|}_R coincide, where ω_s(j) are the components of rsw_{𝔭_j}(χ) in the decomposition along dlog π_i (i ∈ s) defined before the proposition.

items.name: Definition 4.3 (Kato, Definition 7.4): strongly clean
items.statement: Setting of §4.3: A is an excellent regular local ring with fraction field K and residue field ℓ of characteristic p with [ℓ : ℓ^p] = p^c; π₁, …, π_r is part of a regular system of parameters, 𝔭_i = π_iA, R_i = A/𝔭_i, D_j = Σ_{i≠j} V(𝔭_i) ∩ V(𝔭_j) on Spec R_j; χ ∈ H^q(K) is unramified outside ∪ V(𝔭_i) and n_i = sw_{𝔭_i}(χ). χ is strongly clean with respect to A if, for every j with n_j ≥ 1, the image of ω_s(j) in Ω^{q−|s|}_ℓ is non-zero for some s.

items.name: Theorem 4.4 (Kato, Theorem 8.1): Swan conductor after blowing up a point
items.statement: Setting of §4.3: A is an excellent regular local ring with fraction field K and residue field ℓ of characteristic p with [ℓ : ℓ^p] = p^c; π₁, …, π_r is part of a regular system of parameters, 𝔭_i = π_iA, R_i = A/𝔭_i, D_j = Σ_{i≠j} V(𝔭_i) ∩ V(𝔭_j) on Spec R_j; χ ∈ H^q(K) is unramified outside ∪ V(𝔭_i) and n_i = sw_{𝔭_i}(χ). Let f : X → Spec A be the blowup at the closed point and ν the generic point of the exceptional divisor. Then sw_ν(f*χ) ≤ Σ_i n_i, with equality iff χ is strongly clean with respect to A.

items.name: Lemma 4.5: Swan conductors of the residue components
items.statement: Setting of §4.3: A is an excellent regular local ring with fraction field K and residue field ℓ of characteristic p with [ℓ : ℓ^p] = p^c; π₁, …, π_r is part of a regular system of parameters, 𝔭_i = π_iA, R_i = A/𝔭_i, D_j = Σ_{i≠j} V(𝔭_i) ∩ V(𝔭_j) on Spec R_j; χ ∈ H^q(K) is unramified outside ∪ V(𝔭_i) and n_i = sw_{𝔭_i}(χ). Assume n_j = 0, so χ = λ_{π_j}(χ₁, χ₂) in H^q(K_{𝔭_j}) for unique χ₁ ∈ H^q(κ(𝔭_j)), χ₂ ∈ H^{q−1}(κ(𝔭_j)). For i ≠ j, with 𝔭̄_i the image of 𝔭_i in R_j, sw_{𝔭̄_i}(χ₁) ≤ n_i and sw_{𝔭̄_i}(χ₂) ≤ n_i.

items.name: Lemma 4.6: refined Swan conductors of the residue components
items.statement: Setting of §4.3: A is an excellent regular local ring with fraction field K and residue field ℓ of characteristic p with [ℓ : ℓ^p] = p^c; π₁, …, π_r is part of a regular system of parameters, 𝔭_i = π_iA, R_i = A/𝔭_i, D_j = Σ_{i≠j} V(𝔭_i) ∩ V(𝔭_j) on Spec R_j; χ ∈ H^q(K) is unramified outside ∪ V(𝔭_i) and n_i = sw_{𝔭_i}(χ). With r = 2, n₁ = 0, n₂ = n ≥ 1, χ = λ_{π₁}(χ₁, χ₂) along 𝔭₁ and rsw_{𝔭₂}(χ) =[η+ω∧dlog π₁, η′+ω′∧dlog π₁]_{π₂,n}, with η,η′,ω,ω′ respectively of degrees q,q−1,q−1,q−2 in the ordinary differential modules Ω_{R₂}: rsw_{𝔭̄₂,n}(χ₁) = [η̄, −η̄′]_{π̄₂,n} and rsw_{𝔭̄₂,n}(χ₂) = [−ω̄, ω̄′]_{π̄₂,n}, bars denoting reduction modulo 𝔭₁.
items.note: Relates rsw of a class to that of its residue along the exceptional divisor (used in §8).

items.name: Lemma 4.7: detecting forms by δ₁ in top degree
items.statement: Let ℓ be a field of characteristic p with [ℓ : ℓ^p] = p^c and H^{c+1}_p(ℓ) ≠ 0. If α ∈ Ω^q_ℓ satisfies δ₁(aα ∧ dlog b₁ ∧ ⋯ ∧ dlog b_{c−q}) = 0 in H^{c+1}_p(ℓ) for all a ∈ ℓ and b_i ∈ ℓ^×, then α = 0.

items.name: Log-pole residues and the isomorphisms ψ, φ at a blown-up point
items.statement: For a smooth prime divisor D in a smooth variety over a field: 0 → Ω^q_{Y/L} → Ω^q_{Y/L}(log D) →(ρ) i_*Ω^{q−1}_{D/L} → 0, ρ(η + g dlog f) = g|_D. For Y smooth of dimension m over a field L, P₀ ∈ Y(L), the blowup f : Ỹ → Spec O_{Y,P₀} with exceptional Z ≅ P^{m−1}_L: ψ : Ω¹_{Y/L}|_{P₀} ≅ H⁰(Z, O(1)), ψ(dx) = x^{(1)}, and φ : Ω²_{Y/L}|_{P₀} ≅ H⁰(Z, Ω¹_{Z/L}(2)), φ(dx_i ∧ dx_j) = (x_j^{(1)})² d(x_i^{(1)}/x_j^{(1)}).
items.note: Stacks 0FMU; Hartshorne II.8.13.

items.name: Lemma 5.1(1)–(3): 1-forms after blowing up
items.statement: In the setting of §5, fix x ∈ 𝔪 ∖ 𝔪² and π_Z = f*x. (1) π_Z is a local parameter in O_{Ỹ,Z}. (2) For β ∈ Ω¹_{R/L} with image β_{P₀} in Ω¹_{Y/L}|_{P₀}, (f*β)/π_Z ∈ Ω¹_{O_{Ỹ,Z}}(log Z) with residue ψ(β_{P₀})/x^{(1)}. (3) If β_{P₀} ≠ 0, (f*β)/π_Z^r ∉ Ω¹_{O_{Ỹ,Z}}(log Z) for r > 1.

items.name: Lemma 5.1(4)–(5): 2-forms after blowing up
items.statement: In the setting of Lemma 5.1: (4) for α ∈ Ω²_{R/L} with image α_{P₀}, (f*α)/π_Z² ∈ Ω²_{O_{Ỹ,Z}}(log Z) with residue φ(α_{P₀})/(x^{(1)})². (5) If α_{P₀} ≠ 0, (f*α)/π_Z^r ∉ Ω²_{O_{Ỹ,Z}}(log Z) for r > 2.

items.name: Lemma 6.1(1): global log 1-forms on P^n
items.statement: On P^n over a field with coordinates X₀, …, X_n and H = {X₀ = 0}: ρ : H⁰(P^n, Ω¹(log H)(H)) → H⁰(H, O(1)) is an isomorphism; H⁰(P^n, Ω¹(log H)(H)) has basis {d(X_i/X₀) : 1 ≤ i ≤ n} with ρ(d(X_i/X₀)) = −X_i|_H.

items.name: Lemma 6.1(2): H⁰(P^n, Ω¹(2H))
items.statement: On P^n over a field with coordinates X₀, …, X_n and H = {X₀ = 0}: H⁰(P^n, Ω¹(2H)) has basis {(X_i²/X₀²) d(X_j/X_i) = −(X_j²/X₀²) d(X_i/X_j) : 0 ≤ i < j ≤ n}, the n with i = 0 forming the basis of H⁰(P^n, Ω¹(log H)(H)); and 0 → H⁰(Ω¹(log H)(H)) → H⁰(Ω¹(2H)) →(ω ↦ ω|_H) H⁰(H, Ω¹(2)) → 0 is exact, with (X_i²/X₀²) d(X_j/X_i) ↦ X_i² d(X_j/X_i) for 0 < i < j.

items.name: Lemma 6.1(3): global log 2-forms on P^n
items.statement: On P^n over a field with coordinates X₀, …, X_n and H = {X₀ = 0}: ρ : H⁰(P^n, Ω²(log H)(2H)) → H⁰(H, Ω¹(2)) is an isomorphism; H⁰(P^n, Ω²(log H)(2H)) has basis {d(X_i/X₀) ∧ d(X_j/X₀) : 1 ≤ i < j ≤ n} with ρ(d(X_i/X₀) ∧ d(X_j/X₀)) = X_i² d(X_j/X_i).
items.locator: Lemma 6.1, p. 857, (3); proof as corrected by E1
items.note: The proof uses that the X_i² d(X_j/X_i) (0 < i < j) form a basis of H⁰(H, Ω¹(2)); the printed X_i² d(X_j/X_j) is a misprint (E1).

items.name: Lemma 6.2(1): tame part of H¹(P^m ∖ Z)
items.statement: Let F be any field of characteristic p>0 and m≥1. Let E = P^m_F, Z = {X₀ = 0}, π = X₀/X₁, κ(E)_Z the fraction field of the Henselisation of O_{E,Z}, with fil_n H¹(E ∖ Z, Q/Z) pulled back from fil_n H¹(κ(E)_Z). Then fil_0 H¹(E ∖ Z, Q/Z) = H¹(F, Q/Z).

items.name: Lemma 6.2(2): graded pieces of H¹(P^m ∖ Z) for p ∤ n
items.statement: In the setting of Lemma 6.2, for n≥1 with p ∤ n, F ↦ (1/p)δ₁(F̃/X₀^n) is an isomorphism H⁰(Z, O(n)) → gr_n H¹(E ∖ Z, Q/Z), for any lift F̃ ∈ H⁰(E, O(n)), δ₁ the Artin–Schreier map; and rsw_n((1/p)δ₁(F̃/X₀^n)) = [−d(F/X₁^n), nF/X₁^n]_{π,n}.

items.name: Lemma 7.1(1)–(2): lifts of points and tangent vectors
items.statement: Setting of §§1, 3, 7–9: k is a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers O_k, uniformiser π, residue field 𝔽 and absolute ramification index e, and e′ = ep/(p−1). X/k is smooth and geometrically irreducible, 𝒳 → Spec O_k is a smooth model of X (not assumed proper) whose special fibre Y is geometrically irreducible, F is the function field of Y and K^h is the fraction field of a Henselisation of O_{𝒳,Y}. For r ≥ 1 let q_r : 𝒳(O_k) → 𝒳(O_k/π^r). For P ∈ 𝒳(O_k) with reduction P₀ there is a function B(P, r) → T_{P₀}Y, Q ↦ v_r(P, Q), depending on π, such that (1) it factors as q_{r+1} followed by a bijection q_{r+1}(B(P, r)) → T_{P₀}Y; (2) for f ∈ O_{𝒳,P₀}, f(Q) ≡ f(P) + π^r df_{P₀}(v_r(P, Q)) mod π^{r+1}. The lemma rests on Hensel's lemma for the smooth O_k-scheme 𝒳 (each 𝒳(O_k) → 𝒳(O_k/π^r) is surjective).
items.note: Well-known facts; the Hensel lifting for smooth O_k-schemes is imported (SF.4 lifting).

items.name: Lemma 7.1(3): tangent vectors under base change
items.statement: In the setting of Lemma 7.1, let k′/k be finite with ramification index ε, π = c(π′)^ε with c ∈ O_{k′}^×, P′ the base change of P. Then v_{εr}(P′, ·) on q_{εr+1}(B(P′, εr)) restricted from q_{r+1}(B(P, r)) equals c̄^r · v_r(P, ·), identifying T_{P₀}(Y′) = T_{P₀}(Y) ⊗ 𝔽′.

items.name: Lemma 7.3: tangent vectors and strict transforms
items.statement: Setting of §§1, 3, 7–9: k is a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers O_k, uniformiser π, residue field 𝔽 and absolute ramification index e, and e′ = ep/(p−1). X/k is smooth and geometrically irreducible, 𝒳 → Spec O_k is a smooth model of X (not assumed proper) whose special fibre Y is geometrically irreducible, F is the function field of Y and K^h is the fraction field of a Henselisation of O_{𝒳,Y}. Let f : 𝒳̃ → 𝒳 be the blowup at P₀ with exceptional divisor E ≅ P^m_𝔽, U = E ∖ (E ∩ Ỹ) with affine coordinates u_i = x_i^{(1)}/π^{(1)}. Let Q ∈ B(P, r) and P̃, Q̃ the strict transforms, reducing to P̃₀, Q̃₀ ∈ E(𝔽). (1) If r > 1 then Q̃ ∈ B(P̃, r−1) and du_i(v_{r−1}(P̃, Q̃)) = dx_i(v_r(P, Q)). (2) If r = 1 then u_i(Q̃₀) − u_i(P̃₀) = dx_i(v₁(P, Q)).
items.note: E10: with arbitrary local parameters the difference is required. The printed version follows after choosing x_i(P)=0, possible by translation by x_i(P)∈πO_k.

items.name: Theorem 8.1(1): α and β are regular at P₀
items.statement: Setting of §§1, 3, 7–9: k is a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers O_k, uniformiser π, residue field 𝔽 and absolute ramification index e, and e′ = ep/(p−1). X/k is smooth and geometrically irreducible, 𝒳 → Spec O_k is a smooth model of X (not assumed proper) whose special fibre Y is geometrically irreducible, F is the function field of Y and K^h is the fraction field of a Henselisation of O_{𝒳,Y}. Let n > 0, A ∈ fil_n Br X with rsw_n(A) = [α, β]_{π,n}, (α, β) ∈ Ω²_F ⊕ Ω¹_F, and P ∈ 𝒳(O_k) with reduction P₀ ∈ Y(𝔽). Then α and β are regular at P₀.
items.locator: Theorem 8.1, p. 863, (1); = first assertion of Theorem B
items.note: From Theorem 4.1 applied to O_{𝒳,P₀}.

items.name: Theorem 8.1(2) = Theorem B(1): the evaluation formula on B(P, n)
items.statement: Setting of §§1, 3, 7–9: k is a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers O_k, uniformiser π, residue field 𝔽 and absolute ramification index e, and e′ = ep/(p−1). X/k is smooth and geometrically irreducible, 𝒳 → Spec O_k is a smooth model of X (not assumed proper) whose special fibre Y is geometrically irreducible, F is the function field of Y and K^h is the fraction field of a Henselisation of O_{𝒳,Y}. Let n > 0, A ∈ fil_n Br X with rsw_n(A) = [α, β]_{π,n}, (α, β) ∈ Ω²_F ⊕ Ω¹_F, and P ∈ 𝒳(O_k) with reduction P₀ ∈ Y(𝔽). For Q ∈ B(P, n), inv A(Q) = inv A(P) + (1/p) Tr_{𝔽/𝔽_p} β_{P₀}(v_n(P, Q)). In particular, if β_{P₀} ≠ 0 then |A| takes p distinct values on B(P, n).
items.note: The paper's geometric characterisation of the refined Swan conductor. Proved by induction on n through Lemmas 8.3, 8.6 and 8.8.

items.name: Theorem 8.1(3): the bilinear evaluation formula when β = 0
items.statement: Setting of §§1, 3, 7–9: k is a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers O_k, uniformiser π, residue field 𝔽 and absolute ramification index e, and e′ = ep/(p−1). X/k is smooth and geometrically irreducible, 𝒳 → Spec O_k is a smooth model of X (not assumed proper) whose special fibre Y is geometrically irreducible, F is the function field of Y and K^h is the fraction field of a Henselisation of O_{𝒳,Y}. Let n > 0, A ∈ fil_n Br X with rsw_n(A) = [α, β]_{π,n}, (α, β) ∈ Ω²_F ⊕ Ω¹_F, and P ∈ 𝒳(O_k) with reduction P₀ ∈ Y(𝔽). If β = 0 and n > 2, there is γ ∈ Ω¹_Y|_{P₀} such that for Q ∈ B(P, 1) and R ∈ B(Q, n−1), inv A(R) = inv A(Q) − (1/p)Tr α_{P₀}(v₁(P, Q), v_{n−1}(Q, R)) + (1/p)Tr γ(v_{n−1}(Q, R)). If moreover p is odd and 2 < n < e′ + 2 + te for some t ≥ 0 with [k(μ_{p^{t+1}}) : k] prime to p, then for 1 ≤ s < n/2, Q ∈ B(P, s) and R ∈ B(Q, r) with r = n − s, inv A(R) = inv A(Q) − (s/p)Tr α_{P₀}(v_s(P, Q), v_r(Q, R)) + g_{A,Q}(R), with g_{A,Q} : B(Q, r) → p^{−(t+1)}Z/Z continuous and g_{A,Q}(R) = (1/p)Tr γ(v_{n−1}(Q, R)) on B(Q, n−1).
items.note: The extraction records the stated formulas, not a certified proof. Remark 8.2(3)'s original-model D∈fil_{n−1} Br(O_{𝒳,P₀}[1/p]) and the second formula's proof require the E12 repair; a local construction on the blowup does not automatically descend with that bound. Remark 8.2(4) gives the t=0 range when p² does not divide ord A.

items.name: Theorem 8.1(4) = Theorem B(2): p distinct values after one step when β = 0
items.statement: Setting of §§1, 3, 7–9: k is a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers O_k, uniformiser π, residue field 𝔽 and absolute ramification index e, and e′ = ep/(p−1). X/k is smooth and geometrically irreducible, 𝒳 → Spec O_k is a smooth model of X (not assumed proper) whose special fibre Y is geometrically irreducible, F is the function field of Y and K^h is the fraction field of a Henselisation of O_{𝒳,Y}. Let n > 0, A ∈ fil_n Br X with rsw_n(A) = [α, β]_{π,n}, (α, β) ∈ Ω²_F ⊕ Ω¹_F, and P ∈ 𝒳(O_k) with reduction P₀ ∈ Y(𝔽). If β = 0 and α_{P₀} ≠ 0, there is Q ∈ B(P, 1) such that |A| takes p distinct values on B(Q, n−1). This is possible only if p | n (Lemma 2.17).

items.name: Theorem 8.1(5): surjectivity onto Br k[p^{t+1}]
items.statement: Setting of §§1, 3, 7–9: k is a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers O_k, uniformiser π, residue field 𝔽 and absolute ramification index e, and e′ = ep/(p−1). X/k is smooth and geometrically irreducible, 𝒳 → Spec O_k is a smooth model of X (not assumed proper) whose special fibre Y is geometrically irreducible, F is the function field of Y and K^h is the fraction field of a Henselisation of O_{𝒳,Y}. Let n > 0, A ∈ fil_n Br X with rsw_n(A) = [α, β]_{π,n}, (α, β) ∈ Ω²_F ⊕ Ω¹_F, and P ∈ 𝒳(O_k) with reduction P₀ ∈ Y(𝔽). Suppose A has order p^{t+1} in Br X, and either n > e′ + (t−1)e, or n = e′ + (t−1)e and C(α) = C(β) = 0. (i) If β_{P₀} ≠ 0 then |A| : B(P, n − te) → Br k[p^{t+1}] ≅ p^{−(t+1)}Z/Z is surjective. (ii) If β = 0, α_{P₀} ≠ 0, n > e′ + 2 and n ≥ te + 3, there is Q ∈ B(P, 1) with |A| : B(Q, n − te − 1) → Br k[p^{t+1}] surjective.
items.note: Remark 8.2(5): n ≥ te + 3 is only needed when p = e = 2.

items.name: Lemma 8.3: the Swan conductor drops by one along E
items.statement: Setting of §§1, 3, 7–9: k is a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers O_k, uniformiser π, residue field 𝔽 and absolute ramification index e, and e′ = ep/(p−1). X/k is smooth and geometrically irreducible, 𝒳 → Spec O_k is a smooth model of X (not assumed proper) whose special fibre Y is geometrically irreducible, F is the function field of Y and K^h is the fraction field of a Henselisation of O_{𝒳,Y}. f : 𝒳̃ → 𝒳 is the blowup at P₀, E ≅ P^m_𝔽 the exceptional divisor, Z = E ∩ Ỹ, π = π_Ỹ π_E with π_E = f*(x₁), and u_i = x_i^{(1)}/π^{(1)}. If sw(A) = n > 1 and rsw_n(A) = [α, β]_{π,n}, then sw_E(f*A) ≤ n − 1 and rsw_{E,n−1}(f*A) = [α_E, β_E]_{π,n−1}, where β_E ∈ H⁰(E, Ω¹(log Z)(Z)) is the unique element with ρ(β_E) = −ψ(β_{P₀}); explicitly β_E = Σ a_i du_i if β_{P₀} = Σ a_i dx_i. If β_{P₀} ≠ 0 then sw_E(f*A) = n − 1.

items.name: Lemma 8.4: the Swan conductor drops by two when β = 0
items.statement: Setting of §§1, 3, 7–9: k is a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers O_k, uniformiser π, residue field 𝔽 and absolute ramification index e, and e′ = ep/(p−1). X/k is smooth and geometrically irreducible, 𝒳 → Spec O_k is a smooth model of X (not assumed proper) whose special fibre Y is geometrically irreducible, F is the function field of Y and K^h is the fraction field of a Henselisation of O_{𝒳,Y}. f : 𝒳̃ → 𝒳 is the blowup at P₀, E ≅ P^m_𝔽 the exceptional divisor, Z = E ∩ Ỹ, π = π_Ỹ π_E with π_E = f*(x₁), and u_i = x_i^{(1)}/π^{(1)}. Let n > 0 with p | n and s ≥ 0, with n−2(s+1)≥1, sw(A) = n − 2s, rsw_{n−2s}(A) = [α_s, β_s] with α_s = Σ_{i>j} a_{ij} dx_i ∧ dx_j and β_s = s Σ_{i>j} a_{ij} x_j² d(x_i/x_j), a_{ij} ∈ O_{Y,P₀}. Then sw_E(f*A) ≤ n − 2(s+1) and rsw_{E,n−2(s+1)}(f*A) = [α_E, β_E] with α_E = Σ a_{ij}(P₀) du_i ∧ du_j and β_E ≡ (s+1) Σ a_{ij}(P₀) u_j² d(u_i/u_j) mod H⁰(E, Ω¹(log Z)(Z)); equivalently β_E|_Z = (s+1)φ(α_{P₀}) (Remark 8.5). If α_{s,P₀} ≠ 0 then equality holds.
items.note: E11: positive output level is required for rsw. The zero-level terminal case is handled by Lemma 8.7, item 77, using the ordinary residue, not an undefined rsw_0.

items.name: Lemma 8.6: the end game for sw(A) = 1
items.statement: Setting of §§1, 3, 7–9: k is a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers O_k, uniformiser π, residue field 𝔽 and absolute ramification index e, and e′ = ep/(p−1). X/k is smooth and geometrically irreducible, 𝒳 → Spec O_k is a smooth model of X (not assumed proper) whose special fibre Y is geometrically irreducible, F is the function field of Y and K^h is the fraction field of a Henselisation of O_{𝒳,Y}. f : 𝒳̃ → 𝒳 is the blowup at P₀, E ≅ P^m_𝔽 the exceptional divisor, Z = E ∩ Ỹ, π = π_Ỹ π_E with π_E = f*(x₁), and u_i = x_i^{(1)}/π^{(1)}. If sw(A) = 1 and rsw₁(A) = [α, β]_{π,1}, then sw_E(f*A) = 0, and for any linear form F ∈ H⁰(E, O(1)) restricting to ψ(β_{P₀}) on Z, the residue ∂_E(f*A) lies in H¹(E ∖ Z, Q/Z) and equals, modulo H¹(𝔽, Q/Z), the image of F/π^{(1)} under κ(E) → H¹(κ(E), Z/p) →(1/p) H¹(κ(E), Q/Z) (Artin–Schreier).

items.name: Lemma 8.7: the end game for p = 2, sw(A) = 2, β = 0
items.statement: Setting of §§1, 3, 7–9: k is a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers O_k, uniformiser π, residue field 𝔽 and absolute ramification index e, and e′ = ep/(p−1). X/k is smooth and geometrically irreducible, 𝒳 → Spec O_k is a smooth model of X (not assumed proper) whose special fibre Y is geometrically irreducible, F is the function field of Y and K^h is the fraction field of a Henselisation of O_{𝒳,Y}. f : 𝒳̃ → 𝒳 is the blowup at P₀, E ≅ P^m_𝔽 the exceptional divisor, Z = E ∩ Ỹ, π = π_Ỹ π_E with π_E = f*(x₁), and u_i = x_i^{(1)}/π^{(1)}. Suppose p = 2, sw(A) = 2 and rsw₂(A) = [α, 0]_{π,2}. Then sw_E(f*A) = 0; and for any quadratic form F ∈ H⁰(E, O(2)) with dF restricting to φ(α_{P₀}) on Z, ∂_E(f*A) ∈ H¹(E ∖ Z, Q/Z) equals, modulo fil_1 H¹(E ∖ Z, Q/Z), the image of F/(π^{(1)})² under the Artin–Schreier map followed by 1/2.

items.name: Lemma 8.8: Theorem 8.1(2) for n = 1
items.statement: Setting of §§1, 3, 7–9: k is a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers O_k, uniformiser π, residue field 𝔽 and absolute ramification index e, and e′ = ep/(p−1). X/k is smooth and geometrically irreducible, 𝒳 → Spec O_k is a smooth model of X (not assumed proper) whose special fibre Y is geometrically irreducible, F is the function field of Y and K^h is the fraction field of a Henselisation of O_{𝒳,Y}. Let A ∈ fil_1 Br X with rsw₁(A) = [α, β]_{π,1}, P ∈ 𝒳(O_k) with reduction P₀. For Q ∈ B(P, 1), inv A(Q) = inv A(P) + (1/p)Tr_{𝔽/𝔽_p} β_{P₀}(v₁(P, Q)); if β_{P₀} ≠ 0, |A| takes p distinct values on B(P, 1).

items.name: Lemma 8.9: the bilinear formula for β = 0, n > 2
items.statement: Setting of §§1, 3, 7–9: k is a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers O_k, uniformiser π, residue field 𝔽 and absolute ramification index e, and e′ = ep/(p−1). X/k is smooth and geometrically irreducible, 𝒳 → Spec O_k is a smooth model of X (not assumed proper) whose special fibre Y is geometrically irreducible, F is the function field of Y and K^h is the fraction field of a Henselisation of O_{𝒳,Y}. Let n > 2 and A ∈ fil_n Br X with rsw_n A = [α, 0]_{π,n}. There is γ ∈ Ω¹_Y|_{P₀} such that for Q ∈ B(P, 1) and R ∈ B(Q, n−1), inv A(R) = inv A(Q) − (1/p)Tr_{𝔽/𝔽_p}(α_{P₀}(v₁(P, Q), v_{n−1}(Q, R)) + γ(v_{n−1}(Q, R))). If α_{P₀} ≠ 0, there is Q ∈ B(P, 1) on whose disc B(Q, n−1) |A| takes p distinct values.

items.name: Lemma 8.10: the quadratic formula for p = n = 2
items.statement: Setting of §§1, 3, 7–9: k is a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers O_k, uniformiser π, residue field 𝔽 and absolute ramification index e, and e′ = ep/(p−1). X/k is smooth and geometrically irreducible, 𝒳 → Spec O_k is a smooth model of X (not assumed proper) whose special fibre Y is geometrically irreducible, F is the function field of Y and K^h is the fraction field of a Henselisation of O_{𝒳,Y}. Suppose p = 2, A ∈ fil₂ Br X with rsw₂(A) = [α, 0]_{π,2}, α_{P₀} = Σ a_{ij} dx_i ∧ dx_j with a_{ij} ∈ 𝔽. There is γ ∈ Ω¹_Y|_{P₀} such that for Q ∈ B(P, 1), inv A(Q) = inv A(P) + (1/2)Tr_{𝔽/𝔽₂}(Σ a_{ij} dx_i(v₁(P, Q)) dx_j(v₁(P, Q)) + γ(v₁(P, Q))). If α_{P₀} ≠ 0, |A| takes 2 distinct values on B(P, 1).

items.name: Lemma 8.11: realising a prescribed refined Swan conductor by corestricted cyclic algebras
items.statement: Setting of §§1, 3, 7–9: k is a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers O_k, uniformiser π, residue field 𝔽 and absolute ramification index e, and e′ = ep/(p−1). X/k is smooth and geometrically irreducible, 𝒳 → Spec O_k is a smooth model of X (not assumed proper) whose special fibre Y is geometrically irreducible, F is the function field of Y and K^h is the fraction field of a Henselisation of O_{𝒳,Y}. f : 𝒳̃ → 𝒳 is the blowup at P₀, E ≅ P^m_𝔽 the exceptional divisor, Z = E ∩ Ỹ, π = π_Ỹ π_E with π_E = f*(x₁), and u_i = x_i^{(1)}/π^{(1)}. Let β ∈ H⁰(E, Ω¹(log Z)(Z)) and suppose either 0 < n < e′ (set t=0 in this case), or e′ + (t−1)e < n < e′ + te for some t ≥ 1 with ε = [k(μ_{p^{t+1}}) : k] prime to p. Construct C on the generic fibre of an open neighbourhood of P̃₀ in the π-chart of the BLOWN-UP model 𝒳̃, with filtration measured along E: sw_E(C)≤n and rsw_{E,n}(C)=[0,β]_{π,n}. No bound fil_n along the original Y, nor extension to an original-model neighbourhood of P₀, is asserted. Explicitly, with β = Σ b_i du_i, b_i ∈ 𝔽, lifts b̃_i ∈ O_k and K the function field of X: C = cores_{K(μ_{p^{t+1}})/K} Σ_i (1 + p^t b̃_i u_i (ζ_p − 1)^p/(ε(n − te)π^n), u_i)_{p^{t+1}} if p ∤ n − te, and C = cores Σ_i (1 + p^t b̃_i u_i (ζ_p − 1)^p/(επ^n), π)_{p^{t+1}} if p | n − te.
items.note: E12: the original-model assertion contradicts the Swan drop in Lemmas 8.3/8.6. The displayed symbols give the local blown-up-chart construction: their first entries are 1+a u_i with v(a)>0; using {1+a u_i,u_i}={1+a u_i,−a^{-1}} removes the apparent horizontal divisor u_i=0. Shrink away from first-entry zeros. The subsequent descent/filtration claims in the proof of Theorem 8.1(3), second formula, and Remark 8.2(3) require a separate repair; the review does not certify them. The original note incorrectly assigned this lemma to (5).

items.name: The modified Kato filtration fil~_n Br K
items.statement: For K = K^h (and, as the paper notes, any Henselian discrete valuation field of characteristic 0 whose residue field F contains the finite constant field 𝔽): fil~_{−2} = {A ∈ fil_0 Br K : ∂A = 0}; fil~_{−1} = {A ∈ fil_0 : ∂A ∈ H¹(𝔽, Q/Z)}; fil~_0 = fil_0; and for n ≥ 1, fil~_n = {A ∈ fil_{n+1} Br K : rsw_{n+1}(A) ∈ [Ω²_F, 0]_{π,n+1}}. fil_n ⊂ fil~_n, with equality if p ∤ n + 1 (Lemma 2.17); on Br K[p] the two filtrations coincide for n ≥ 0 if e′ < p or Ω²_F = 0. Pulled back to Br X it gives fil~_n Br X.
items.note: The paper's new filtration: analogous to Matsuda's non-logarithmic filtration on H¹. Owned here with its comparisons in §10; Theorem A identifies it with Ev_n.

items.name: Lemma 9.1: fil~_n Br X ⊂ Ev_n Br X
items.statement: Setting of §§1, 3, 7–9: k is a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers O_k, uniformiser π, residue field 𝔽 and absolute ramification index e, and e′ = ep/(p−1). X/k is smooth and geometrically irreducible, 𝒳 → Spec O_k is a smooth model of X (not assumed proper) whose special fibre Y is geometrically irreducible, F is the function field of Y and K^h is the fraction field of a Henselisation of O_{𝒳,Y}. For n ≥ −2, fil~_n Br X ⊂ Ev_n Br X.
items.note: From Proposition 3.1 (n ≤ 0), and Theorem 8.1(2) with Lemma 2.16 (n ≥ 1).

items.name: Lemma 9.2: elements outside fil~_{n−1} take p values on some disc
items.statement: Setting of §§1, 3, 7–9: k is a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers O_k, uniformiser π, residue field 𝔽 and absolute ramification index e, and e′ = ep/(p−1). X/k is smooth and geometrically irreducible, 𝒳 → Spec O_k is a smooth model of X (not assumed proper) whose special fibre Y is geometrically irreducible, F is the function field of Y and K^h is the fraction field of a Henselisation of O_{𝒳,Y}. Let n ≥ 1 and A ∈ fil~_n Br X ∖ fil~_{n−1} Br X. There are a finite unramified k′/k and P ∈ 𝒳(O_{k′}) such that |A| takes p distinct values on B(P, n). In particular A ∉ Ev_{n−1} Br X.
items.locator: Lemma 9.2, p. 879, proof as corrected by E2
items.note: Uses Lang–Weil and Hensel. In the proof, res_{k′/k}A ∈ fil_{n+1}, not fil_n (E2).

items.name: Lemma 9.3: constancy on discs forces fil~_n
items.statement: Setting of §§1, 3, 7–9: k is a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers O_k, uniformiser π, residue field 𝔽 and absolute ramification index e, and e′ = ep/(p−1). X/k is smooth and geometrically irreducible, 𝒳 → Spec O_k is a smooth model of X (not assumed proper) whose special fibre Y is geometrically irreducible, F is the function field of Y and K^h is the fraction field of a Henselisation of O_{𝒳,Y}. For n ≥ 0, Ev_n Br X ⊂ {A : for all finite unramified k′/k and P ∈ 𝒳(O_{k′}), |A| is constant on B(P, n+1)} ⊂ fil~_n Br X.

items.name: Corollary 9.4: Theorem A for n ≥ 0, with unramified extensions only
items.statement: Setting of §§1, 3, 7–9: k is a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers O_k, uniformiser π, residue field 𝔽 and absolute ramification index e, and e′ = ep/(p−1). X/k is smooth and geometrically irreducible, 𝒳 → Spec O_k is a smooth model of X (not assumed proper) whose special fibre Y is geometrically irreducible, F is the function field of Y and K^h is the fraction field of a Henselisation of O_{𝒳,Y}. For n ≥ 0 the three sets of Lemma 9.3 are equal: Ev_n Br X = {A : |A| constant on B(P, n+1) for all finite unramified k′/k and P ∈ 𝒳(O_{k′})} = fil~_n Br X.
items.note: Gives Theorem A(3)–(4).

items.name: Lang–Weil: points over large finite fields
items.statement: A geometrically irreducible variety over a finite field 𝔽 has 𝔽′-points for every sufficiently large finite extension 𝔽′/𝔽 (indeed #V(𝔽_{q^r}) = q^{r dim V} + O(q^{r(dim V − 1/2)})).
items.note: The current WC.5 contract is smooth-projective; a previous paper route is not authority to enlarge it to arbitrary varieties. Route 2 is rejected until the general Lang–Weil input is placed under a source-qualified owner or explicitly added by an authorized design.

items.name: Hochschild–Serre for H¹ of a variety over a finite field
items.statement: For a geometrically connected variety Y over a finite field 𝔽, with geometric base change Ȳ, restriction gives an exact sequence 0→H¹(𝔽,Q/Z)→H¹(Y,Q/Z)→H¹(Ȳ,Q/Z); the analogous kernel statement holds for the constant sheaf Z/p^r, r≥1. The last map need not be surjective as written.
items.note: PAPER-HARPAZ-WITTENBERG-16 routes the scheme Hochschild–Serre sequence to SF.2.

items.name: Bright 2015, Lemma 5.15: torsors with geometrically maximal order are geometrically connected
items.statement: Let Y be a smooth geometrically connected variety over a finite field and T → Y a Z/m-torsor whose class has order m in H¹(Ȳ, Z/m). Then T is geometrically connected, hence (being smooth) geometrically irreducible.

items.name: Lemma 9.5: Ev_{−2} and Ev_{−1} tested on unramified extensions
items.statement: Setting of §§1, 3, 7–9: k is a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers O_k, uniformiser π, residue field 𝔽 and absolute ramification index e, and e′ = ep/(p−1). X/k is smooth and geometrically irreducible, 𝒳 → Spec O_k is a smooth model of X (not assumed proper) whose special fibre Y is geometrically irreducible, F is the function field of Y and K^h is the fraction field of a Henselisation of O_{𝒳,Y}. Ev_{−2} Br X ⊂ {A : |A| is zero on 𝒳(O_{k′}) for all finite unramified k′/k} ⊂ fil~_{−2} Br X, and Ev_{−1} Br X ⊂ {A : |A| is constant on 𝒳(O_{k′}) for all finite unramified k′/k} ⊂ fil~_{−1} Br X.
items.locator: Lemma 9.5, p. 880, statement as corrected by E3
items.note: The printed statement begins "For every r ≥ 1", but r does not occur (E3). For the prime-to-p part this goes back to Colliot-Thélène–Saito (Remark 9.6).

items.name: Corollary 9.7: Theorem A for n = −2, −1
items.statement: Setting of §§1, 3, 7–9: k is a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers O_k, uniformiser π, residue field 𝔽 and absolute ramification index e, and e′ = ep/(p−1). X/k is smooth and geometrically irreducible, 𝒳 → Spec O_k is a smooth model of X (not assumed proper) whose special fibre Y is geometrically irreducible, F is the function field of Y and K^h is the fraction field of a Henselisation of O_{𝒳,Y}. Ev_{−2} Br X = {A : |A| zero on 𝒳(O_{k′}) for all finite unramified k′/k} = fil~_{−2} Br X, and Ev_{−1} Br X = {A : |A| constant on 𝒳(O_{k′}) for all finite unramified k′/k} = fil~_{−1} Br X.
items.note: Gives Theorem A(1)–(2).

items.name: Corollary 9.8(1): Ev_n for n ≤ 0 is stable under base change
items.statement: Setting of §§1, 3, 7–9: k is a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers O_k, uniformiser π, residue field 𝔽 and absolute ramification index e, and e′ = ep/(p−1). X/k is smooth and geometrically irreducible, 𝒳 → Spec O_k is a smooth model of X (not assumed proper) whose special fibre Y is geometrically irreducible, F is the function field of Y and K^h is the fraction field of a Henselisation of O_{𝒳,Y}. Let k′/k be finite. For −2 ≤ n ≤ 0, A ∈ Ev_n Br X implies res_{k′/k}(A) ∈ Ev_n Br X_{k′}.

items.name: Corollary 9.8(2): how Ev_n rescales under ramified base change
items.statement: Setting of §§1, 3, 7–9: k is a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers O_k, uniformiser π, residue field 𝔽 and absolute ramification index e, and e′ = ep/(p−1). X/k is smooth and geometrically irreducible, 𝒳 → Spec O_k is a smooth model of X (not assumed proper) whose special fibre Y is geometrically irreducible, F is the function field of Y and K^h is the fraction field of a Henselisation of O_{𝒳,Y}. Let k′/k be finite with ramification index e (here e = e(k′/k)), n ≥ 1, A ∈ Ev_n Br X ∖ Ev_{n−1} Br X, rsw_{n+1}(A) = [α, 0]_{π,n+1}, and if α = 0, rsw_n(A) = [α′, β′]_{π,n}. Then res_{k′/k}(A) lies in: Ev_{e(n+1)−1} ∖ Ev_{e(n+1)−2} if α ≠ 0; Ev_{en} ∖ Ev_{en−1} if α = 0 and p ∤ e; Ev_{en−1} ∖ Ev_{en−2} if α = 0, α′ ≠ 0 and p | e; Ev_{en−1} if α = α′ = 0 and p | e. (If p ∤ n + 1 then α = 0, Remark 9.9.)
items.locator: Corollary 9.8, p. 881, (2), with Remark 9.9; proof as completed by E4
items.note: When α = 0, A ∉ fil~_{n−1} forces β′ ≠ 0; the printed proof of the case p ∤ e only uses rsw_n(A) ≠ 0 (E4).

items.name: Lemma 10.1, corrected: cup products with K× realise the Swan conductor
items.statement: Let K be a Henselian DVF of characteristic 0 containing a primitive p-th root of unity, with imperfect residue field F, e′ = v_K(p)p/(p−1). If χ ∈ H¹_p(K) has sw(χ) = n, there is y ∈ K^× with sw({χ, y}) = n and, if n > 0, y can be chosen with {χ, y} ∉ fil~_{n−1} Br K[p].
items.note: Case analysis via Bloch–Kato's description of graded pieces ([K, (4.2.1)–(4.2.2), Proposition 4.1, Lemma 4.3]). E13: replace the printed unit restriction by K×; the proof's uniformizer choices are then allowed. Proposition 10.2 needs exactly this weaker conclusion.

items.name: Proposition 10.2: fil~ is not induced from H¹
items.statement: Suppose K contains a primitive p-th root of unity and the filtrations fil~_n Br K[p] and fil_n Br K[p] (n ≥ 0) do not coincide. Then there is no increasing filtration Fil_n H¹(K, Z/p) such that, for all n ≥ 0, fil~_n Br K[p] is generated by {Fil_n H¹(K, Z/p), K^×}.
items.note: The hypothesis forces F imperfect, which Lemma 10.1 needs.

items.name: Abbes–Saito ramification filtrations and the conductors f_K, f_K^log
items.statement: For G = Gal(K̄/K) of a Henselian DVF with possibly imperfect residue field, Abbes and Saito's non-logarithmic and logarithmic filtrations (G^a)_{a∈Q≥0} and (G^a_log). For χ ∈ H^q_p(K): f_K(χ) = inf{a > 0 : χ ∈ ker(H^q_p(K) → H^q(G^a, (Z/p)(q−1)))} and f_K^log likewise with G^a_log; for q = 1 these are Abbes–Saito's (log) conductors ([AS, Propositions 6.4, 9.5]). fil_0 H^q_p(K) = {f_K ≤ 1} = {f_K^log ≤ 0}. The proof of Proposition 10.9 also cites from [AS] the inclusion G^{pa}_{L,log} ⊂ G^a_log for a totally ramified L/K of degree p.
items.note: The source's general-q tilde notation at level zero is not defined; use Kato's fil_0 (which equals fil~_0 in degree 2). Positive-index conductors and the passage from infima to boundary membership need the Abbes–Saito continuity results, not merely a definition.

items.name: Kato–Saito: Kato's filtration on H¹ is the logarithmic Abbes–Saito filtration
items.statement: For a Henselian DVF K (any residue field), Kato's filtration fil_n on H¹(K) coincides with the filtration induced by the logarithmic ramification filtration G^a_log. In positive characteristic, Matsuda's non-logarithmic variant coincides with the one induced by G^a (Saito, Corollary 3.3).
items.note: Context for Propositions 10.3, 10.8 and 10.9.

items.name: Proposition 10.3: the non-logarithmic conductor of a character
items.statement: Suppose K contains a primitive p-th root of unity and χ ∈ H¹_p(K). For all n ≥ 0, f_K(χ) ≤ n + 1 ⟺ (χ ∈ fil_{n+1} H¹_p(K) and rsw_{n+1}(χ) = [α, 0]_{π,n+1} with α ∈ Ω¹_F).
items.note: The proof is a sketch: generators of the graded pieces (Bloch–Kato) plus Lemmas 10.4–10.7 via [AS, Lemma 6.6]. The brief asks for the full case check. In positive characteristic it is [Saito, Corollary 3.3].

items.name: Lemma 10.4: f_K of K(π^{1/p})
items.statement: If K ∋ ζ_p and χ ∈ H¹(K, Z/p) corresponds to K(π^{1/p})/K, then f_K(χ) = e′ + 1.
items.note: O_L = O_K[π^{1/p}] and [AS, Lemma 6.6].

items.name: Lemma 10.5: f_K of a ferociously ramified Kummer extension
items.statement: If K ∋ ζ_p, x ∈ O_K^× with x̄ ∉ F^p, and χ corresponds to K(x^{1/p})/K, then f_K(χ) = e′.

items.name: Lemma 10.6: f_K of K((1 + xπ^m)^{1/p}), p ∤ m
items.statement: If K ∋ ζ_p, x ∈ O_K^×, 0 < m < e′, p ∤ m, and χ corresponds to K((1 + xπ^m)^{1/p})/K, then f_K(χ) = e′ + 1 − m.
items.note: ϖ = (1 + xπ^m)^{1/p} − 1, 1 = rm + sp; ϖ^rπ^s is a uniformiser.

items.name: Lemma 10.7: f_K of K((1 + xπ^{np})^{1/p}), x̄ ∉ F^p
items.statement: If K ∋ ζ_p, x ∈ O_K^× with x̄ ∉ F^p, 0 < np < e′, and χ corresponds to K((1 + xπ^{np})^{1/p})/K, then f_K(χ) = e′ − np.

items.name: Proposition 10.8: fil~ is not the non-logarithmic Abbes–Saito filtration
items.statement: Suppose K contains a primitive p-th root of unity and F is not perfect. Then it is not true that fil~_n Br K[p] = {χ ∈ Br K[p] : f_K(χ) ≤ n + 1} for all n ≥ 0; the equality fails for n = e′ − 1, witnessed by {ψ, π} with ψ ↔ K(x̃^{1/p}), x ∈ F ∖ F^p.
items.locator: Proposition 10.8, p. 886, proof as corrected by E5
items.note: The printed proof says the failure is at n = e′; its argument shows n = e′ − 1 (E5).

items.name: Proposition 10.9: fil~ is not the logarithmic Abbes–Saito filtration
items.statement: Suppose Ω²_F ≠ 0. It is not true that, for all finite extensions L/K, fil~_n H²_p(L) = {χ ∈ H²_p(L) : f_L^log(χ) ≤ n}.
items.locator: Proposition 10.9, p. 886, proof as corrected by E6
items.note: Witness: A = (x̃, ỹ)_p with dx/x ∧ dy/y ≠ 0, restricted to a totally ramified L/K of degree p such as K(π^{1/p}); the printed 'any wildly ramified extension of degree p' is too broad (E6).

items.name: Bloch–Kato: gr⁰ H² is non-zero at an ordinary prime
items.statement: Let V_𝔭 be smooth proper over a p-adic field with smooth proper model 𝒱 whose special fibre Y is ordinary. The spectral sequences E₂^{s,t} = H^s(Ȳ, ī*R^t j̄_* Z/p^r) ⇒ H^{s+t}(V̄_𝔭, Z/p^r) ([BK, 0.2]) define filtrations on H^q(V̄_𝔭, Z/p^r), Z_p and Q_p; if H⁰(V, Ω²) ≠ 0 then gr⁰ H²(V̄_𝔭, Q_p) ≠ 0 ([BK, Theorem 0.7(iii)]), hence gr⁰ H²(V̄_𝔭, Z/p^r) ≠ 0 for some r.
items.note: Bloch–Kato's ordinary-reduction theorem, degree-two consequence. A source-qualified owner for its comparison with the nearby-cycle filtration remains to be established; generic nearby cycles and de Rham–Witt coefficients alone do not supply it.

items.name: Invariance of étale cohomology of proper varieties under extension of algebraically closed fields
items.statement: For V proper over a field L̄ algebraically closed and L̄ ⊂ Ω algebraically closed, H^q(V, Z/n) → H^q(V_Ω, Z/n) is an isomorphism ([Milne, Corollary VI.2.6]).
items.locator: Proofs of Theorems C and D, pp. 887, 889
items.note: Proper base change, an SF.2 export.

items.name: Lemma 11.1: no global 1- and 2-forms on Y forces fil_0 = everything
items.statement: Setting of §§1, 3, 7–9: k is a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers O_k, uniformiser π, residue field 𝔽 and absolute ramification index e, and e′ = ep/(p−1). X/k is smooth and geometrically irreducible, 𝒳 → Spec O_k is a smooth model of X (not assumed proper) whose special fibre Y is geometrically irreducible, F is the function field of Y and K^h is the fraction field of a Henselisation of O_{𝒳,Y}. If H⁰(Y, Ω¹_Y) = H⁰(Y, Ω²_Y) = 0 then fil_0 Br X = Br X.
items.note: Not used later; from Theorem 8.1(1).

items.name: Lemma 11.2: H⁰(Ω¹_Y) = 0 and e < p − 1 force fil_0 = everything
items.statement: Setting of §§1, 3, 7–9: k is a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers O_k, uniformiser π, residue field 𝔽 and absolute ramification index e, and e′ = ep/(p−1). X/k is smooth and geometrically irreducible, 𝒳 → Spec O_k is a smooth model of X (not assumed proper) whose special fibre Y is geometrically irreducible, F is the function field of Y and K^h is the fraction field of a Henselisation of O_{𝒳,Y}. If H⁰(Y, Ω¹_Y) = 0 and e < p − 1, then fil_0 Br X = Br X.
items.note: Lemma 2.17 for p ∤ n; Lemma 2.19 to pass from sw = n > e′ with p | n to pA.

items.name: Lemma 11.3: H¹(Ȳ, Z/p) = 0 makes the p-part tame-constant
items.statement: Setting of §§1, 3, 7–9: k is a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers O_k, uniformiser π, residue field 𝔽 and absolute ramification index e, and e′ = ep/(p−1). X/k is smooth and geometrically irreducible, 𝒳 → Spec O_k is a smooth model of X (not assumed proper) whose special fibre Y is geometrically irreducible, F is the function field of Y and K^h is the fraction field of a Henselisation of O_{𝒳,Y}. If H¹(Ȳ, Z/p) = 0 then fil~_{−1} Br X{p} = fil_0 Br X{p}.

items.name: Lemma 11.4: vanishing of H¹ specialises
items.statement: Let 𝒳 → Spec O_k be smooth and proper with geometrically integral generic fibre X, and n ≥ 1. If H¹(X̄, Z/n) = 0 then the special fibre satisfies H¹(Ȳ, Z/n) = 0.
items.note: A statement of étale cohomology of schemes: proper base change H¹(Y′) ≅ H¹(𝒳′) and injectivity of H¹(𝒳′) → H¹(X′) for normal connected 𝒳′ ([SGA 1, I.10.2]).

items.name: Colliot-Thélène–Skorobogatov, Proposition 2.4: prime-to-p evaluation at good places
items.statement: As used: in the situation of Theorem D, for 𝔭 ∉ S of residue characteristic p, every A ∈ Br V of order prime to p has constant evaluation on V(L_𝔭).
items.locator: Proof of Theorem D, p. 889 ([CTSk, Proposition 2.4])
items.note: Imported as a cited theorem with CTSk's exact hypotheses; the prime-to-p analogue of Lemmas 11.2–11.3, via Bright 2015 §5.

items.name: Torsion-free Pic V̄ kills H⁰(Ω¹) generically and at almost all places
items.statement: If V is smooth proper over a number field with Pic V̄ torsion-free then H¹(V, O_V) = 0 and hence, by Hodge theory, H⁰(V, Ω¹_V) = 0; for a smooth proper model 𝒱 over O_S, upper semicontinuity gives H⁰(𝒱(𝔭), Ω¹) = 0 for all 𝔭 outside a finite set; and the Kummer sequence gives H¹(V̄, Z/n) = 0 for all n.
items.note: Bundle requiring separate Picard-scheme, characteristic-zero Hodge-symmetry, Kummer and higher-dimensional semicontinuity inputs. A curve/Picard-focused Jacobian layer does not by itself discharge all smooth proper varieties in this statement. Source-qualified ownership and geometric hypotheses remain a closure gap.

items.name: Remark 11.5 and Remark 1.6(2): for K3 surfaces the set in Theorem D(4) is empty
items.statement: If V is a K3 surface and 𝒱 → Spec O_𝔭 is a smooth proper model, then 𝒱(𝔭) is a K3 surface (ω trivial because Pic 𝒱 ≅ Pic V; h⁰(O) = h²(O) = 1 by Serre duality and h¹(O) = 0 by constancy of χ), so H⁰(𝒱(𝔭), Ω¹) = 0 ([Huybrechts, Theorem 9.5.1]). For a K3 surface over Q, the only places in the Brauer–Manin obstruction are the archimedean place, the primes of bad reduction and 2.

items.name: Ordinary Kähler differentials and their universal derivation
items.statement: For a commutative R-algebra S, Ω_{S/R}=I/I² for I=ker(S⊗_R S→S); D:S→Ω_{S/R} is the universal R-derivation. Every R-derivation S→M factors uniquely through an S-linear map Ω_{S/R}→M.
items.locator: §2.3; §§4–8; underlying carrier, not the log enhancement
items.note: Mathlib/RingTheory/Kaehler/Basic.lean:153,198,274,289 at 082e2d37e8b0463410cdb532e111cd43d5a66174. Does not provide the log point, Cartier operator, or scheme blowup formulas.

items.name: Cohomology of an abelian sheaf on a site
items.statement: For a category C with Grothendieck topology J and abelian sheaf F, under HasSheafify and HasExt, H^n(F)=Ext^n(Z_J,F), n≥0.
items.note: Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Sites/SheafCohomology/Basic.lean:59 at 082e2d37e8b0463410cdb532e111cd43d5a66174. Hypercohomology, coefficient twists, direct images, spectral-sequence edges and Brauer identifications remain distinct dependencies.

items.name: Derived category of an abelian category
items.statement: For an abelian category C with a chosen derived-category localization, D(C) is the localization of integer-graded cochain complexes at quasi-isomorphisms; the localization functor Q sends quasi-isomorphisms to isomorphisms and D(C) is triangulated.
items.locator: §1.4 coefficients as complexes; §2.2 spectral sequences and §2.5 Kummer triangle
items.note: Mathlib/Algebra/Homology/DerivedCategory/Basic.lean:69–105,169–179 at 082e2d37e8b0463410cdb532e111cd43d5a66174. Abstract carrier only, not an étale six-functor or nearby-cycle implementation.

items.name: Kummer short exact sequence of discrete Galois modules at an invertible exponent
items.statement: For a field K, n a natural number with n invertible in K, the inclusion μ_n(K^s)→(K^s)× and nth power map give a short exact sequence of discrete continuous AbsoluteGaloisGroup K-modules, written additively.
items.note: TauCeti/FieldTheory/GaloisCohomology/Coefficients.lean:90,107,195 at f790474821cf4256814db967cb154e7af3d0c369. Does not cover p-primary étale roots-of-unity Kummer in characteristic p, nor prove the cohomological Brauer comparison.

routes.reason: SF.2 owns étale cohomology of schemes: proper and smooth base change, localisation, and (by the Česnavičius and Harpaz–Wittenberg routes) Brauer purity and the scheme Hochschild–Serre sequence. The paper's general étale inputs belong there: Gabber's affine analogue of proper base change for Henselian pairs, invariance of the étale cohomology of proper varieties under extension of algebraically closed fields, purity Br 𝒳 = Br X ∩ Br O_{𝒳,Y} for smooth 𝒳, the Hochschild–Serre sequence for H¹ over a finite field, and Lemma 11.4 (vanishing of H¹ specialises, via proper base change and SGA 1, I.10.2).

WC.5 owns point-count bounds over finite fields, and PAPER-HARPAZ-WITTENBERG-16 already routes the Lang–Weil–Nisnevich estimate for arbitrary geometrically irreducible varieties there. This paper uses the same estimate in Lemmas 9.2 and 9.5.

RP.2 owns the Brauer–Manin pairing and 'effective tests for a specified finite subgroup of the Brauer group'. The one-place test (a class with non-constant local evaluation obstructs weak approximation; one with surjective evaluation does not obstruct the Hasse principle) is such a test and is how Theorem C is applied.

routes.title: Local fields and ramification, Part II: Kato's Swan conductors for imperfect residue fields
routes.brief:
First prerequisite: Local fields and ramification (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/LocalFieldsRamification), whose Layer 3 upper-numbering filtration this extends; do not replan it. The new object is Kato's theory of Swan conductors for H^q of a Henselian discrete valuation field K whose residue field F of characteristic p may be imperfect (Kato 1989, Contemp. Math. 83), in both mixed and equal characteristic, together with Bright–Newton's refinements (Invent. Math. 234 (2023), §§2, 4, 9–10).

Coefficients and cohomology:
- Kato's coefficients (Z/n)(r) = μ_m^{⊗r} ⊕ W_sΩ^r_log[−r] and H^q_n(R), with the triangle (Z/n)(1) → G_m → G_m.
- V^q_n(A) = H^q(R_ét, i*Rj_*(Z/n)(q−1)), its functoriality and products.
- Bloch–Kato's filtration U^m on M^q_r = i*R^q j_*(Z/p^r)(q), with gr⁰ ≅ W_rΩ^q_log ⊕ W_rΩ^{q−1}_log.

The filtration and the maps:
